skill.name: adhd-mode
skill.description: Use when the user asks for ADHD mode or focus mode, mentions overwhelm, stuck starting, too many open threads or options, losing the plot after an interruption, executive-function friction, or needs low-friction multi-turn work. Structures replies with Answer/Action/Artifact/Project contracts, working-set limits (Active 1 · Ready ≤2), interruption recovery, Clean/Flow/Zen long-form modes, and explicit ND-safe directives (persona alone is not enough). Disable on "stop ADHD mode", "normal mode", or "stop focus mode".
skill.summary: Structures AI responses to reduce cognitive load, limit active work, and support interruption recovery.
skill.author: fuzzywigg

content.user_title: Reduce Cognitive Load with ADHD Mode
content.value_statement: Complex conversations can create too many choices, unclear priorities, and difficult restarts. This skill structures replies around one active task and clear recovery cues.
actual_capabilities: Places the answer, action, artifact, or project status first.
Limits the working set to one active item and two ready items.
Breaks blocked tasks into a small first action with a stopping condition.
Restores context after interruptions with a short reorientation line.
Offers Clean, Flow, and Zen structures for different response lengths.
Disables the mode when the user requests normal responses.
limitations: It does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or therapy.
It changes response structure but cannot manage external reminders or applications.
Its default structure may not suit users who prefer unrestricted exploration.
It depends on the host retaining conversation context for effective recovery.

use_cases.title: Start an Overwhelming Task
use_cases.description: Turn a vague or difficult task into one manageable action with a clear stopping point.

use_cases.title: Resume Interrupted Work
use_cases.description: Recover the current goal, verified progress, and next action without replaying the full conversation.

use_cases.title: Structure Detailed Learning
use_cases.description: Organize technical explanations into scannable sections while preserving evidence, nuance, and necessary depth.

prompt_templates.title: Choose One Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ADHD mode. I feel stuck on [task]. Give me one small action and a clear stopping condition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for immediate help starting

prompt_templates.title: Map a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ADHD mode to map [project]. Define completion, choose one active step, and list no more than two ready steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a project with limited working scope

prompt_templates.title: Resume After Interruption
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume our work on [goal]. State the verified position and one next action before adding any necessary detail.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from Repeated Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: We tried [approaches], but [problem] remains. Separate known facts from assumptions, identify one likely issue, and propose one diagnostic.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging after multiple unsuccessful attempts

output_examples.input: I need to prepare the report, but I cannot start.
output_examples.output: Active: Open the report document and write three section headings. Stop when the headings exist; content can wait.

output_examples.input: Where were we before the interruption?
output_examples.output: You are here: finalize the budget brief, the totals are verified, and the next action is reviewing the recommendation paragraph.

output_examples.input: Should I use the quick fix or redesign the component?
output_examples.output: Choose the quick fix when the deadline is fixed and the defect is isolated. Redesign only if the same limitation affects planned work.

best_practices: State the goal and any important constraints when enabling the mode.
Use quick controls such as "one thing," "map it," or "resume" when your needs change.
Request more detail when brevity would remove evidence, safety information, or essential nuance.
anti_patterns: Do not use the mode as medical guidance or as a substitute for professional care.
Do not hide multiple urgent tasks behind an artificial single priority.
Do not force short answers when the requested deliverable requires complete detail.

faq.question: Does this skill diagnose ADHD?
faq.answer: No. It provides accessible response structure without diagnosing users or requiring a diagnosis.

faq.question: How do I enable the mode?
faq.answer: Ask for ADHD mode or focus mode, or describe difficulty starting, prioritizing, or resuming work.

faq.question: How do I disable the mode?
faq.answer: Say "stop ADHD mode," "normal mode," or "stop focus mode."

faq.question: Will every response be very short?
faq.answer: No. The skill reduces cognitive load while preserving the detail needed for a complete and safe answer.

faq.question: Can it help after an interruption?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize the goal, verified state, and next action in a short reorientation line.

faq.question: Does it use external tools or network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is instruction-only and does not require executables, packages, network requests, or filesystem access.
